target.title: fix(agents): tighten findSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bash-tools.schemas.ts` uses `Type.Number` for three fields that semantically require integer values — `yieldMs` (milliseconds), `offset` (log position), and `limit` (entry count). Fractional values like `offset=10.5` silently pass `Type.Number` validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

## Root Cause

`Type.Number` in TypeBox accepts any JavaScript number including floats. For fields whose semantics are inherently integer-valued, invalid input survives the schema gate.

## Fix

Change three `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` in `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts`. `Type.Integer` uses `Number.isInteger()` internally, rejecting fractional values at the schema boundary.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts` | 3× `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Number.isInteger behavior (used by Type.Integer internally)

```
$ node -e "..."

yieldMs (milliseconds before backgrounding):
  ✅ 10000  → Integer (valid)    ✅ accepted
  ❌ 10.5   → float  (invalid)   ❌ REJECTED by Type.Integer

offset (log position):
  ✅ 100    → Integer (valid)    ✅ accepted
  ❌ 10.5   → float  (invalid)   ❌ REJECTED by Type.Integer

limit (log length):
  ✅ 50     → Integer (valid)    ✅ accepted
  ❌ 5.3    → float  (invalid)   ❌ REJECTED by Type.Integer
```

Before this PR, all 6 values pass `Type.Number` validation. After this PR, the 3 fractional values are rejected at the schema gate.

### Vitest

Existing agent tool schema tests continue to pass unchanged. The change is a schema-level tightening — no runtime behavior changes for valid integer inputs.
